title: Recompute the Provisioning Plan
subtitle: New start, revised SLA - re-derive the dates
scenario: Two things changed: the start date moved, and the hardware SLA gained slack (SD-2). Rebuild Sam Rivera's plan by re-deriving each due date from the authoritative start and the revised policy - never from the old, cached dates.
input:
Onboarding record: Sam Rivera (H-4022), Logistics Coordinator, amended start SD.
Owners: accounts -> IT Provisioner; hardware -> IT Provisioner; access -> Facilities Coordinator; payroll -> Payroll Specialist.
Revised SLA policy v1.1.0 (business days before start): accounts SD-2, hardware SD-2, access SD-1, payroll SD-3.
Re-derive every due date from the authoritative start and the revised policy.
instructions: Create one row per task: accounts, hardware, access, payroll.
Set each owner from the owners list.
Set each due from the REVISED policy (hardware is now SD-2).
Return a JSON array of the four rows, then validate.
copilotPrompt: Rebuild the provisioning plan for a moved start and revised policy. Four rows (accounts, hardware, access, payroll) with owner and due. Hardware is now SD-2; re-derive all dates from the authoritative start.
successMessage: Plan recomputed. Every due date is re-derived from the authoritative start and revised policy.
editorHelper: Re-derive from the start - never reuse the cached dates.

sections.title: Cached dates are stale dates
sections.body: When the start moves, any due date computed from the old start is wrong. Because deadlines are SD-relative, you re-derive them from the authoritative start rather than editing calendar dates by hand.

sections.title: Two changes, one recompute
sections.body: The start moved and the hardware SLA changed. Both flow through the same recompute: apply the current policy to the current start, and the plan is right by construction.

sections.title: Owners are stable
sections.body: The mess is dates, not accountability. Each task keeps its single owner; only the due dates move.

sections.title: What you produce here
sections.body: A recomputed plan the four branches run against - correct for the moved start and the revised hardware SLA.

fieldGuide.hint: Revised policy: accounts SD-2, hardware SD-2, access SD-1, payroll SD-3.

realWorld.soloRebuildPath: You'd recompute each due date from the new start rather than shifting old dates by hand and hoping.

tools.powerAutomate: recompute due dates with addDays from the current start date
tools.zapier: re-run the date-math step against the amended start
tools.python: recompute due = start - sla_days for every task

takeaway.heading: Plan recomputed
points: You re-derived every due date from the authoritative start, not cached dates.
The moved start and the revised hardware SLA both flowed through one recompute.
Owners stayed stable; only the deadlines moved.
Hardware now sits at SD-2 with its added slack.
The workflow can now recompute the plan whenever the start or policy changes.
